## Downloads

| Dataset | CSV | JSON | What it contains |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Features | [CSV](data/public/csv/features.csv) | [JSON](data/public/json/features.json) | Common feature index and coordinates |
| Access points | [CSV](data/public/csv/access-points.csv) | [JSON](data/public/json/access-points.json) | Mile ranges, coordinates, and amenities |
| Locks | [CSV](data/public/csv/locks.csv) | [JSON](data/public/json/locks.json) | Numbers, names, mileposts, and coordinates |
| Relationships | [CSV](data/public/csv/relationships.csv) | [JSON](data/public/json/relationships.json) | Nearby features and reference matches |
| Sources | [CSV](data/public/csv/sources.csv) | [JSON](data/public/json/sources.json) | URLs, attribution, and artifact provenance |
| Towpath | — | [GeoJSON](data/public/towpath.geojson) | Canonical route geometry |

The common feature schema is deliberately small: `id`, `name`, `feature_type`,
`mile`, optional `mile_end`, WGS84 coordinates, and `source_ids`. Dedicated files
retain details that do not belong in every feature record.

`source_ids` joins to the source registry. In CSV, multiple IDs are separated with
`|`; JSON retains them as arrays. Amenity fields are blank or `null` when an access
point has no matched NPS recreation-guide record—unknown does not mean false.

## Regenerate

```console
uv sync
uv run python -m canawler.build
uv run pytest
```

Routine generation uses only committed files under `data/reference/` and does not
contact external services. See the [repository README](https://github.com/derailable/canawler#readme)
for reference-refresh and site-rendering commands.
